relationship.statement: For small swings without drag, a pendulum's period depends only on its length and gravity, not on the bob's mass or release angle.
assumptions: Small-angle approximation: restoring torque is proportional to angle.
Air resistance and pivot friction are neglected.
String is massless and Earth gravity is fixed at 9.81 m/s^2.

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot to the center of the test bob.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the test pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle from vertical when released at time zero.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Gravitational acceleration held constant at 9.81 m/s^2.

quantities.label: Test period
quantities.meaning: Time for one full back-and-forth swing of the test pendulum.

quantities.label: Ref period
quantities.meaning: Time for one full swing of the fixed 1 m reference pendulum.

quantities.label: Test angle
quantities.meaning: Current angle of the test pendulum from vertical.

quantities.label: Ref angle
quantities.meaning: Current angle of the reference pendulum from vertical.

quantities.label: Test weight
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational force pulling on the test bob.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var g = 9.81; var twoPi = 2 * Math.PI; var refLen = 1.0; var refMass = 1.0; var refAmp = 15; var L = inputs.length; var m = inputs.mass; var amp = inputs.angle; var testPeriod = twoPi * Math.sqrt(L / g); var refPeriod = twoPi * Math.sqrt(refLen / g); var testThetaRad = (amp * Math.PI / 180) * Math.cos(twoPi * t / testPeriod); var refThetaRad = (refAmp * Math.PI / 180) * Math.cos(twoPi * t / refPeriod); var testAngle = testThetaRad * 180 / Math.PI; var refAngle = refThetaRad * 180 / Math.PI; var testX = -1.1 + L * Math.sin(testThetaRad); var testY = 2.5 - L * Math.cos(testThetaRad); var refX = 1.1 + refLen * Math.sin(refThetaRad); var refY = 2.5 - refLen * Math.cos(refThetaRad); var testSize = 0.2 + 0.15 * m; var refSize = 0.2 + 0.15 * refMass; var testWeightY = testY - 0.12 * m; var refWeightY = refY - 0.12 * refMass; var testWeightN = m * g; var isLonger = L > 1.05; var isShorter = L < 0.95; var isSameLengthDiff = !isLonger && !isShorter && (Math.abs(m - refMass) > 0.1 || Math.abs(amp - refAmp) > 0.5); return { testPeriod: testPeriod, refPeriod: refPeriod, testAngle: testAngle, refAngle: refAngle, testX: testX, testY: testY, testSize: testSize, testWeightY: testWeightY, testWeightN: testWeightN, refX: refX, refY: refY, refSize: refSize, refWeightY: refWeightY, isLonger: isLonger, isShorter: isShorter, isSameLengthDiff: isSameLengthDiff }; }

lesson.title: What changes a pendulum's swing period?
lesson.description: Compare a test pendulum against a fixed reference pendulum side by side. Adjust length, mass, and release angle to see which changes the swing time.
lesson.instructions: Start with both pendulums matched, then change one slider at a time. Watch whether the test angle wave drifts out of phase with the reference wave on the plot.
lesson.goal: Only string length (and gravity) changes a small-angle pendulum's period; mass and release angle do not.
